chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Said from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from Al-Hasan ibn Abi al-Halab (Al-Halabi) from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said:

Regarding a man who bought a slave girl and she had not yet menstruated: He said, 'If she is young, and pregnancy is not expected, there is no waiting period (istibra') upon her, and he may have intercourse with her if he wishes.' And if she has reached puberty but has not menstruated, then there is a waiting period upon her.' He said, 'And I asked him about a man who bought a slave girl while she was menstruating: He said, 'When she becomes pure (from menstruation), let him touch her if he wishes.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on istibra for a purchased slave girl who has not yet menstruated?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Istibsar clarifies the application of 'istibra' (waiting period) in the context of purchasing a female slave, distinguishing between pre-pubescent girls where pregnancy is unlikely and those who have reached puberty but lack menstruation. It further specifies that if the slave is purchased while menstruating, the waiting period commences only after her menses cease, reflecting the juristic principle of linking legal status to biological markers. This ruling underscores the practical implications for marital and ownership rights in Shia fiqh, ensuring clarity in lineage and pregnancy confirmation.
